scope: Read-only ARM paired-kernel source audit of the installed LSM annotation
findings: The paired verifier converts reads through PTR_TO_BTF_ID and listed untrusted pointer types to BPF_PROBE_MEM/BPF_PROBE_MEMSX and increments num_exentries.
The paired ARM JIT add_exception_handler registers EX_TYPE_BPF for each such BPF load; ex_handler_bpf clears the destination and advances PC by four bytes on a handled fault.

The paired native emitter copies native words then resolves relocation records. Its emission interface carries image/index/payload/program/final_ip; native memory accesses retain their ordinary CPU fault behavior.

The archived no_null_check native P and compiled B both read ctx[0] then file+32. The stock-verifier treatment of B gives its BTF pointer access a recoverable load semantic, while the copied native LDR retains the architectural data-abort semantic.

The design faithfulness obligation includes matching object, boundary and fault behavior. O3 must establish actual physical-entry pointer validity for every plain native access, or faithfully retain the fault in verifier-visible execution. O4 must preserve the selected memory/fault semantics when composing physical entry and emitted P.
V owns the universal O1/O3/O4 premise statement. C owns the same-kernel stock-BPF LSM baseline. A retains installed-stage accounting and paired ARM source evidence.
disposition: Coordinator/operator model decision requested for generic fault qualification; application producers can express probe reads before submission where source semantics require them. Kernel selftest sources and current running captures retain their published bytes.
